resources.string: This needs a permission that is still off.
So a name can become a phone number.
So Kawkab can place a call after you tap.
So a reminder can be written on the calendar.
So Kawkab can tell you when it needs you.
So you can speak instead of type.
Kawkab looks at the screen and taps only after you allow this. It stays on this phone.
So a request can finish while the screen is off.
On Android 13 and newer: open App info, tap the menu shown here, then Allow restricted settings. Then turn the accessibility service on.
Allow the phone to keep Kawkab running
On Nothing OS, also allow unrestricted background use in the app\'s battery settings, or the phone may stop Kawkab.
Android will not ask again. In App info, open Permissions and turn this on, then come back.
Also set the power button: Settings → System → Gestures (or Buttons) → Press and hold power button → Digital assistant. Nothing OS may set it to the power menu.
Or use the “Ask Kawkab” Quick Settings tile or home-screen shortcut.
So a long-press of the power button opens Kawkab over any app.
